title_card.title: Rome
title_card.note: Watch the Eternal City rise, burn and rise again

cards.title: 2,779 years
cards.years: from a hilltop village to the Eternal City
cards.note: Illustrative reconstruction · data: Overture Maps, OpenStreetMap contributors, Copernicus

events.title: Hills above a river
events.body: Shepherds and farmers live on wooded hills beside a bend of the Tiber

events.title: Romulus and Remus
events.body: Abandoned by the river, twin boys are found and fed by a she-wolf, says the legend

events.title: The founding
events.body: Legend says Romulus draws the city's boundary on the Palatine Hill and names Rome after himself

events.title: Kings of Rome
events.body: Seven kings, the story goes. The marshy valley below the hills is drained and becomes the Forum

events.title: The Republic
events.body: The last king is expelled. Rome is now ruled by the Senate and elected consuls

events.title: The Gauls sack Rome
events.body: Gallic warriors storm in from the north and burn the city. Only the Capitoline holds out

events.title: Mistress of the Mediterranean
events.body: After the wars with Carthage, wealth and slaves pour into a fast-growing city

events.title: The Ides of March
events.body: Julius Caesar is stabbed to death by senators at a meeting in the Theatre of Pompey

events.title: Augustus
events.body: Rome's first emperor claims he found a city of brick and left it a city of marble

events.title: The Great Fire
events.body: Fire burns for six days near the Circus Maximus. Much of Rome is destroyed. Nero is blamed

events.title: The Colosseum opens
events.body: Up to 50,000 spectators watch 100 days of games to celebrate its opening

events.title: A city of a million
events.body: Perhaps a million people live here, the largest city in the world at the time

events.title: The Pantheon
events.body: Hadrian's temple gets its great concrete dome, still the largest unreinforced dome on Earth

events.title: The Baths of Caracalla
events.body: Vast public baths open, with room for over 1,500 bathers at a time

events.title: The Aurelian Walls
events.body: With enemies at Italy's borders, Rome builds 19 km of new walls

events.title: Constantine
events.body: The first Christian emperor. Churches like Old St. Peter's begin to rise

events.title: The Visigoths sack Rome
events.body: Alaric's army enters through the Salarian Gate at night. Rome is plundered for three days

events.title: The Vandals
events.body: A second sack, this time for two weeks. The word 'vandalism' comes from it

events.title: The end of the Western Empire
events.body: The last emperor in the West is deposed. Rome's population collapses

events.title: The aqueducts are cut
events.body: During a siege the aqueducts are broken. The hills empty and people move down to the river

events.title: Charlemagne crowned
events.body: The Pope crowns the Frankish king emperor in Old St. Peter's

events.title: The Normans burn Rome
events.body: Robert Guiscard's army frees the pope and sets the city ablaze from the Campus Martius to the Lateran

events.title: City of towers
events.body: Noble families build fortified towers and fight each other in the streets

events.title: The popes leave
events.body: The papacy moves to Avignon. Rome shrinks to perhaps 20,000 people among the ruins

events.title: The Renaissance
events.body: Popes return, rebuild and invite the great artists of the age

events.title: A new St. Peter's
events.body: The 1,200-year-old basilica is pulled down. Its replacement will take 120 years

events.title: The Sack of Rome
events.body: Mutinous imperial troops storm the walls. The Swiss Guard dies defending the Pope

events.title: Michelangelo's dome
events.body: The great dome of St. Peter's is completed, 26 years after Michelangelo's death

events.title: Baroque Rome
events.body: Bernini's fountains and squares transform the city. The Four Rivers Fountain fills Piazza Navona

events.title: St. Peter's Square
events.body: Bernini's colonnade embraces the square like two open arms

events.title: The Roman Republic
events.body: Revolutionaries declare a republic. French troops besiege the Janiculum and restore the Pope

events.title: The breach of Porta Pia
events.body: Italian troops break through the walls. Rome becomes part of Italy, and soon its capital

events.title: A new capital
events.body: Ministries, boulevards and new districts rise inside and beyond the old walls

events.title: The Vittoriano
events.body: A vast white monument to Italy's first king opens, 50 years after unification

events.title: Via dei Fori Imperiali
events.body: A broad avenue is cut through the ancient forums, demolishing a neighbourhood

events.title: The bombing of San Lorenzo
events.body: Allied bombers strike the rail yards. Around 1,500 people are killed in the district

events.title: The Italian Republic
events.body: Italians vote to end the monarchy

events.title: The Olympic Games
events.body: Rome hosts the Summer Olympics, the 'Dolce Vita' years

events.title: The Great Jubilee
events.body: Some 25 million pilgrims visit the city

events.title: Rome today
events.body: Nearly three million people live in the Eternal City
